task_production_rates.name: Verify tread protection in place
task_production_rates.notes: ~1.5 min per tread for verification/repair. Faster than initial install (25 EA/hr) since protection likely already in place from riser spec. If installing new: use 25 EA/hr rate.

task_production_rates.name: Install landing floor protection
task_production_rates.notes: Canvas drop cloth layout at landings. Standard protection rate.

task_production_rates.name: Mask walls for spray containment
task_production_rates.notes: Tape and paper/Tape & Drape along walls. Standard masking rate.

task_production_rates.name: Set up baluster spray containment
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. Cardboard shields behind balusters, junction taping. Time varies significantly with baluster count and stairwell configuration. 45 min is typical for standard 39-62 baluster system.

task_production_rates.name: Solvent clean iron balusters (SSPC-SP 1)
task_production_rates.notes: ~1 min/EA. Wipe each baluster with solvent-soaked rag. Non-negotiable first step for all iron balusters. Fast but critical.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff-sand powder-coated iron balusters
task_production_rates.notes: ~2 min/EA. Scotch-Brite pad, 180-220 grit equivalent. Conformable pad follows profile. Creates mechanical tooth.

task_production_rates.name: Sand wood balusters per substrate
task_production_rates.notes: SS_BARE: full 150-220 grit sand. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: scuff sand 150-180. Turned balusters ~1.5-1.7x slower due to complex profile. Square: ~5 min/EA bare, ~3 min/EA factory. Turned: ~7.5 min/EA bare, ~5 min/EA factory.

task_production_rates.name: Sand newel posts per substrate
task_production_rates.notes: SS_BARE: ~12 min/newel full sand. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: ~7.5 min/newel scuff. Larger than balusters with more detail (caps, rosettes, flutes).

task_production_rates.name: Sand handrails per substrate
task_production_rates.notes: SS_BARE: full sand on 4 surfaces (~1.5 min/LF). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: scuff sand (~1 min/LF). Slower than flat trim due to 4-surface access.

task_production_rates.name: Sand base rails per substrate
task_production_rates.notes: Conditional. 3 surfaces — slightly faster than handrail.

task_production_rates.name: Remove sanding dust
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. Tack cloth all railing surfaces, vacuum treads/landings. Slightly longer than riser spec due to more component surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes and sand smooth
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr for combined fill + sand on wood components. Primarily balusters and newels. QT3: obvious holes. QT4: all visible. QT5: all holes regardless of size.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk newel junction joints
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr per newel. ~7.5 min per newel for 2-3 joints (newel-to-tread, newel-to-handrail). Caulk application + tooling.

task_production_rates.name: Remove handrail brackets (label and bag)
task_production_rates.notes: ~5 min per bracket. Remove screws, label bracket, bag hardware, mark location on wall. QT4+ only. Typical: 3-5 brackets per handrail run.

task_production_rates.name: Prime balusters
task_production_rates.notes: Brush prime. Square: ~4 min/EA (same as riser). Turned: ~7 min/EA (midpoint of 5-10 doctrine range). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. Iron balusters use DTM primer at same rates.

task_production_rates.name: Prime newel posts
task_production_rates.notes: ~15 min/newel brush prime. Larger surface, more detail than balusters. Caps, rosettes, flutes require careful coverage.

task_production_rates.name: Prime handrails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr brush prime. ~25% slower than flat trim (80 LF/hr) due to 4-surface access. QT4+: painting horizontally (brackets removed) is faster.

task_production_rates.name: Prime base rails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Slightly faster than handrail (3 surfaces vs 4). Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Light sand primer for adhesion
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. 220 grit light sand all primed surfaces. More surfaces than riser spec. Tack cloth after.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on balusters
task_production_rates.notes: Square: ~4 min/EA per coat (midpoint of 3-5 doctrine range). Turned: ~7 min/EA per coat (midpoint of 5-10 doctrine range). Includes junction cut-in at baluster-handrail connection. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on newel posts
task_production_rates.notes: ~15 min/newel per coat. Larger and more detailed than balusters. Caps, rosettes, flutes, all 4 sides.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on handrails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr brush finish. 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). ~25% slower than flat trim (85 LF/hr). QT4+: painting horizontally reduces drip risk and increases speed slightly.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on base rails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. 3 surfaces — slightly faster than handrail. Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on balusters
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr spray finish. ~2.5x faster than brush for square balusters. HVLP preferred. Containment must be in place. All profiles spray at similar rates (profile complexity affects brush, not spray).

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on newel posts
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr spray. ~3x faster than brush (4 EA/hr). Larger target, easy to spray but more material.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on handrails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr spray finish. ~3x faster than brush. Light passes on all 4 surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on base rails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr spray. Slightly faster than handrail (3 surfaces). Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Clean work area between coats
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove dust/debris from treads and landings.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect previous coat
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. More components to inspect than riser spec (balusters + newels + handrails + base rails). QT3: quick scan. QT4: systematic, mark defects. QT5: critical with light.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle per system. QT3: spot sand nibs only. QT4: full 220 grit all components. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit. Significantly more surface than riser spec due to baluster count. Junction nibs at baluster-handrail critical at QT4+.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and repair marked defects
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Varies by QT — scope of repair increases with tier.

task_production_rates.name: Spot coat patched areas
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Touch-up patched areas before next full coat.

task_production_rates.name: Tack cloth all surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle per system. More surfaces than riser spec — tack all balusters, newels, handrails.

task_production_rates.name: Final quality inspection
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. Check all components, junctions, caulk lines, finish quality. More components than riser spec.

task_production_rates.name: Feel test on handrails
task_production_rates.notes: ~30 sec/LF. Run hand along handrail, check for nibs, rough spots, drip ridges. QT5 only. Must be glass-smooth.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up defects from final inspection
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. Correct remaining defects. Feather into surrounding finish.

task_production_rates.name: Apply polyurethane topcoat on handrails
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Optional QT5. Single coat water-based poly. Thin, even application. Allow enamel to fully cure first (24-48 hours).

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall handrail brackets
task_production_rates.notes: ~6 min/bracket. Reinstall from labeled bags, align to marks, secure, touch-up. QT4+ only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove spray containment
task_production_rates.notes: Per system. Remove cardboard shields, Tape & Drape. Spray method only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove wall masking
task_production_rates.notes: Score tape edge, pull at 45-degree angle. Spray method only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove floor protection at landings
task_production_rates.notes: Fold and remove canvas drops.

task_production_rates.name: Remove tread protection
task_production_rates.notes: ~1.5 min per tread. Score tape edges, remove Ram Board carefully. May be deferred if tread work follows.

task_production_rates.name: Clean tools and equipment
task_production_rates.notes: Per session. Clean brushes (including German round), spray equipment. Slightly longer than riser spec due to specialty brushes.

all_components.rationale: All railing components accessible from treads or adjacent floor/landing. H1 applies to ALL railing tasks. The difficulty is detail complexity and component count, not height access.

quality_tier_modifiers.applies_to: qt_scaled tasks only (inspection, sanding, repair, fill)
quality_tier_modifiers.does_not_apply_to: application tasks (brush/spray finish, prime) — application quality is NOT tiered

baluster_profile_modifier.notes: Ratio of midpoint times: turned 7 min / square 4 min ≈ 1.75. Applies to ALL baluster-specific tasks (prep sand, prime, finish). Does NOT apply to newel, handrail, or base rail tasks. Does NOT apply when railing_type=iron_and_wood (iron balusters are always straight/scrollwork — profile complexity is constant).
baluster_profile_modifier.source: Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2: square 3-5 min/EA, turned 5-10 min/EA

round_configurations.notes: May also include MOD_STRL_PRIME if SS_BARE or SS_POWDER_COATED (4 total coats, 3 interstages).

estimation_notes.quad_uom: Baluster/newel tasks use EA, handrail/base rail tasks use LF, interstage/inspect/cleanup use FIXED. Total labor = baluster_hours + newel_hours + handrail_hours + base_rail_hours + fixed_hours.
estimation_notes.baluster_count_driver: Baluster count is the DOMINANT cost driver. A system with 62 turned balusters at 7 min/EA × 3 coats = 1,302 minutes (~22 hours) of baluster painting alone. Always validate baluster count input.
estimation_notes.access_staging_overhead: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 5.6: 15-40% of total stairway project time consumed by access staging. This is a project-level overhead — not modeled per-task.
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush_tradeoff: Spray is 2.5-3x faster for application but requires 45+ min containment setup. Break-even at approximately 20-25 balusters. Below that, brush is more efficient overall.
estimation_notes.two_person_technique: Two-person baluster technique (one each side simultaneously) is not modeled as a separate task — captured in rate variability for large systems.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS.
